summary: This sermon explores Sabbath as the first thing God called holy in creation—not a place but a sanctuary in time. The preacher argues that God embedded a rhythm of work and rest into the fabric of creation, and that regular Sabbath practice is essential for intimacy with God and sustainable ministry. He presents ten Old Testament principles for Sabbath observance, emphasizing it as a gift rather than a legalistic burden.
key_points: God's first holy thing was time itself—the seventh day of rest
Sabbath rest is embedded in creation's structure across cultures
Jesus modeled prioritizing time alone with the Father despite busy ministry
Ten practical Sabbath principles: no regular work, rest, prepare ahead, decide/eliminate, nurture relationships, celebrate, remember, keep it holy
Our bodies will get Sabbath whether we choose it or not; better to embrace it as God's gift
big_idea: God created Sabbath as holy time set apart in the fabric of creation for rest and intimacy with Him, and intentionally practicing it fills us with power for ministry and gives us a foretaste of heaven.
title: Sabbath Principles
